resources.string: Read and send your texts here

LightDecoder can connect to Google Messages on your phone the same way \"Messages for web\" does in a browser. You can then read your conversations here, reply, see reactions, and HEIC stickers that arrive are decoded into the sticker inbox automatically, without notification access.

LightDecoder emulates Messages for web using Google\'s private, undocumented protocol (through the open-source libgm library). Google does not offer this to other apps, and using it this way is against Google\'s Terms of Service. Google could stop it from working at any time, and could take action on the Google account used. Only continue if you accept that risk.
Your data stays on this device

Messages are stored only on this phone, in LightDecoder\'s private storage, and are never backed up to the cloud. The sign-in session is encrypted with a key kept in Android\'s keystore. LightDecoder has no servers and no analytics: it only talks to Google, exactly like Messages for web does.
You confirm it on your phone

You sign in to the Google account that Google Messages on your phone uses. LightDecoder then shows an emoji, and nothing is linked until you tap the same emoji in Google Messages on your phone. LightDecoder cannot do that step for you.

While connected, a notification is always shown, with a Disconnect button. Disconnect stops the connection and keeps the link for later. Unpair, in the link\'s settings here, removes the link from your phone too and deletes the session; you can also remove \"LightDecoder\" under Device pairing in Google Messages on your phone at any time.
I understand, and I want to link my own Google Messages

Sign in to the Google account that Google Messages on your phone uses. Only the sign-in cookies Messages for web needs are kept; this browser is wiped right after. If Google says this browser may not be secure, use \"Paste cookies\" instead.
Google\'s sign-in page could not be loaded. Check the internet connection and try again.
Only Google\'s sign-in pages open here.

Advanced: on a computer, sign in to messages.google.com, open the browser\'s developer tools, and copy the cookies for google.com and messages.google.com. LightDecoder reads a cookie export (JSON), a Cookie header, or \"Copy as cURL\". Only paste your own cookies: they give full access to that Google account.
No Google cookies found in that text.
The cookies were removed from the clipboard. If your keyboard keeps a clipboard history, delete them there too: LightDecoder cannot reach it.
This phone\'s web component (Android System WebView) is not available right now, so Google\'s sign-in page cannot open. Try again later, or use \"Paste cookies\".
Google Messages on your phone now asks to link a device and shows a few emoji. Tap the one shown here. If Google Messages is on this same phone, remember the emoji, then switch to Google Messages.
Waiting for you to tap it on your phone. Nothing is linked until you do.
Emoji to tap on your phone: %1$s
LightDecoder is now connected to Google Messages on your phone. Your recent conversations are being imported. A notification shows while it is connected; tap Disconnect there to stop.

Set up the link to read and send messages here.
Waiting for you to confirm on your phone.
Messages already imported can still be read. New messages and sending need a connection.
Connecting to Google Messages on your phone.
New messages arrive here as they come in.
Google Messages is open in another browser or app, so it is paused here. Tap \"Use here\" to switch it back.
Google cannot reach your phone. Check that it is on and online. Messages are sent once it answers.
The link was removed on your phone, or the Google account signed out. Set it up again to reconnect. Imported messages are kept.
Google no longer accepts this sign-in. Set the link up again with a fresh sign-in. Imported messages are kept.
The connection stopped because of an error. The activity log in the link\'s settings has details.
The link only connects while its notification, with its Disconnect button, can be shown. Turn on LightDecoder\'s notifications to connect.

While the link is connected, LightDecoder always shows a notification with a Disconnect button, so you can see it is running and stop it at any time. It cannot connect without it. Turn on LightDecoder\'s notifications (at least \"Google Messages link\") in system settings.
This phone is not linked to Google Messages yet. Set up the link first.
Not connected to your phone right now. Turn on \"Stay connected\" and try again.
The sign-in did not give the cookies Messages for web needs. Sign in again, or paste your cookies.
Google did not accept this sign-in. It may have expired, or the account is signed out. Sign in again.
No phone with Google Messages was found for this Google account. On your phone, open Google Messages, make sure it is signed in to the same account (Device pairing in its settings), and try again.
Your phone did not answer the link request. Make sure it is on and online and that Google Messages is up to date, then try again. If this account has several phones, pairing may not work.
You tapped a different emoji on your phone, so nothing was linked. Try again and tap the emoji shown here.
Linking was cancelled, on your phone or here. Nothing was linked.
Your phone did not confirm in time. Try again, and tap the emoji on your phone within three minutes.
A link attempt is still running. Wait a moment, then try again.
That link attempt expired. Start again.
Your phone is not responding. Check that it is on and online. It may still finish what was asked once it answers.
The connection closed before your phone answered. Try again.
Google could not find that. It may have been deleted on your phone.
That request could not be sent as it is.
That file is too large to send or download.
Your phone could not send this message.
The link was removed on your phone, or the Google account signed out. Set it up again to reconnect.
LightDecoder\'s notifications are turned off, so the link cannot connect: it always shows a notification with a Disconnect button while connected.
Something went wrong in the link. Try again; if it keeps happening, the activity log in the link\'s settings may help.
Nothing yet. Lines appear here when the link connects, syncs or fails. They never contain message text, names, numbers or keys.
Keeps a connection to your phone open in the background, with a notification you can disconnect from.
Off by default, because Google Messages on your phone already notifies.
Decode stickers into the sticker inbox
Android may pause the connection to save battery. Exempting LightDecoder from battery optimization keeps it connected.
LightDecoder is exempt from battery optimization.
This phone did not open that settings screen.

LightDecoder is removed from the paired devices on your phone, and the sign-in session on this device is deleted. To use it again, you set it up from the start. A kept archive is deleted if you later link a different phone or Google account.
Also delete the local message archive
Messages and pictures kept on this device from the earlier link. The sticker inbox is not affected.
All conversations, messages and media stored on this device are deleted. Your phone is not linked, so nothing changes there. The sticker inbox is kept.
